title: O(N) Iteration False Positive
summary: iter() in try_state, on_runtime_upgrade, and BoundedVec is structurally safe. Do not flag as O(N) anti-pattern.
remedy: Whitelist try_state, migrations, and BoundedVec iter() calls from O(N) iteration bans.

title: Off-chain fixed-digest iteration false positive
summary: fee_envelope_vectors::hex iterates only over a fixed-size digest in an off-chain evidence generator; it never scans consensus storage or runtime-controlled state.
remedy: Use the narrow deos-bypass: bounded-iter annotation on the fixed digest iterator while retaining the global consensus-state iteration rule.

title: Benchmarking before Experiment Prepared gate
summary: EXP-0003 B0/C1 current-load benchmarks ran while the record remained Proposed and before the complete lifecycle harness and candidate identities were frozen.
remedy: Treat outputs as non-authoritative rehearsal, finish and freeze the complete B0/C1 harness, transition to Prepared, then rerun; assert status before benchmark commands.

title: Runtime ceiling advanced without every generated benchmark range
summary: The P32 binding left C6 geometry benchmarks at the prior 0..=2 range, compared the maximum-Opening selector against four predicates even though four Opening predicates produce eight evaluation units, and declared 40 funding entries without populating them in the atomic benchmark. The owner was unreachable and its setup omitted one claimed maximum dimension.
remedy: Whenever a runtime bound advances, audit every physical benchmark range and prove each special owner is selected by a realizable context whose benchmark setup and postconditions materialize every claimed maximum dimension.

title: Subtracting separately generated Weight owners is not a valid atomic split
summary: A measured full-cycle Running branch had lower estimated ProofSize than the sum of separately generated queue scan/probe/consume owners because proof keys overlap. Component-wise subtraction therefore cannot derive an inner atomic owner even when RefTime subtraction appears valid.
remedy: Benchmark each non-overlapping ownership boundary directly. The remaining Running/Suspended and nonmaximum-Opening owners must measure the inner plan/evaluate/commit/post-placement atom after separately owned queue discovery/state loading, never derive it by subtracting independent generated estimates.

title: Mixed predicate evaluation units are not a monotonic benchmark axis
summary: A single 0..=8 Suspended-head benchmark axis changed physical predicate composition at unit five: current predicates decreased while frozen Opening predicates increased. RefTime peaked near the composition boundary and then fell, causing generated linear regression to discard the axis and underprice realizable intermediate branches.
remedy: Keep the monotonic current-only 0..=4 owner and benchmark Opening-heavy branches under a separate direct owner materializing the worst realizable one-Opening/three-current composition; do not encode changing physical compositions as one linear parameter.

title: Persistent funding wait solves the wrong User process-lifetime boundary
summary: Replacing current-Step apoptosis with ActorFundingWait prevented immediate death but retained nonviable process state indefinitely and added wait authority, ingress wake, and scheduler reinsertion. It also failed the stronger invariant that an economically admitted multi-Step Cycle must finish without reclassification between Steps.
remedy: Evaluate User viability only while Idle. Derive a fixed-size full-Cycle economic envelope at Contract mutation, reserve retry-inclusive Cycle plus minimal-cleanup capacity at Opening, carry it through Q1, and perform custody-neutral minimal apoptosis only at a nonviable boundary.

title: Whole-pipeline control liveness does not require prepaying future Action effects
summary: The first EXP-0019 correction combined Actor control and Task-effect maxima into one retry-inclusive Cycle balance reserve. That conflated deterministic machine service with uncertain transaction-like Actions, created a persistent run fee ledger, and charged authority for effects that might never be invoked.
remedy: Charge Trigger plus complete bounded Pipeline Machine control upfront at ready Opening, charge each invoked Action from current valid-actual effect evidence, treat unfunded non-invocation as FundingUnavailable, and retain no run machine balance ledger.

title: Configured NextBlock timing is not implemented by the current Actors cutoff
summary: EXP-0018 and architecture prose described T+1 as the production baseline, but external AddressEvent/Manual readiness is queued in block N and execute_cycle snapshots NextQueueTicket only during the same block on_idle pass; runtime tests explicitly execute repeated same-block transfers. A generated I4 Weight/Wasm identity therefore does not establish the specified NextBlock causal baseline.
remedy: Implement and test the prepass cutoff/NextBlock source contract before constructing or measuring SameBlockExternal; bind timing and provenance into runtime configuration and admission identity.

title: Lifecycle envelope used as FIFO stop owner
summary: The complete lifecycle admission envelope was treated as the next live FIFO head requirement, overstating control Weight and making stop classification non-falsifiable against the scheduler admission point.
remedy: Classify a post-probe stop with queue-consume maximum plus stored Step control plus reachable cleanup; include scan/probe only when measuring before those costs are consumed, and keep lifecycle admission separate.

title: Transient Cargo Wasm mistaken for canonical evidence mutation
summary: Release-profile assurance rebuilt the repository-local Wasm side artifact and then reported that transient Cargo output as mutation of the caller-selected canonical production Wasm, despite every behavioral gate passing.
remedy: Snapshot the canonical Wasm before Cargo validation, restore it atomically on success or failure, and compare the restored bytes while source, Weight, and metadata identities remain independently checked.

title: Partial control cell mistaken for complete frame authority
summary: The 171-byte admission strip and then the 198-byte identity/hot cell were each treated as complete authority before tracing all reconstruction inputs; the latter still omitted the immutable admission certificate, dual coexisting process/Trigger wakeup pointers, and an explicit unsignaled placement.
remedy: Before naming a compact cell complete, prove round-trip reconstruction for identity, hot state, admission, ready/waiting/unsignaled placement, and coexisting memberships; derive only fields whose source remains uniquely available at every transition.

title: Step atom mistaken for complete Pipeline Opening
summary: An EXP-0025 benchmark called execute_current_step_and_place directly with the useful-signal latch still set, then treated Idle/pending output and cycle_nonce 0 as a complete User Opening branch. It bypassed canonical Pipeline Opening consumption and made the 5,652-proof projection invalid.
remedy: A complete-path benchmark must traverse the canonical FIFO and Pipeline Opening transition, then assert nonce advancement, latch consumption, run state, final placement, fees, and events; direct Step atoms remain branch components only.

title: Placement-sized state hold introduced semantic event drift
summary: The direct C32 branch initially priced the actual encoded eligible_at value, so Ready-to-Unsignaled released eight held units and emitted a Balances event absent from A0 despite otherwise exact state and fee equivalence.
remedy: Price the maximum bounded placement envelope for frame-resident control fields, as A0 prices maximum hot/run geometry, and require exact differential event tests across every physical placement transition.

title: Concurrent production-Wasm probes confounded RefTime
summary: The direct-prefix and rejected-head frame-omni-bencher processes were first launched in parallel, making both CPU timing models non-comparable even though proof and storage ownership remained deterministic.
remedy: Run decision-bearing production-Wasm benchmarks sequentially on the same host; retain parallel runs only as discarded rehearsals and bind recorded artifacts to sequential reruns.

title: Capacity-violating sparse fixture mistaken for scale evidence
summary: The first EXP-0025 sparse-read fixture staged 10,000 future cells plus 100 due cells even though the runtime admits at most 10,000 active Actors, so its 10,100-cell population could not represent a realizable scheduler state.
remedy: Keep sparse scheduler fixtures within MaxActiveActors; the corrected population is 9,900 future plus 100 due, and acceptance claims must bind total registered authority as well as the due subset.

title: Benchmark unit-test geometry did not admit the production benchmark range
summary: Actors Crossing benchmarks declared 128-member/page production ranges, but the runtime-benchmarks test runtime retained 8 User members, 16-member pages, and 16-Actor worker limits. Full benchmark tests therefore failed in setup or exercised a different topology even though production-Wasm benchmarks used the larger runtime constants.
remedy: Under runtime-benchmarks, bind mock Crossing page/User/worker bounds to the declared 128-member geometry and keep ordinary tests dynamic in configured bounds; require the complete benchmark-feature suite, not only focused benchmark tests.

title: Source-preserving intent was mistaken for retained benchmark identity
summary: After the focused EXP-0025 benchmarks, later source and validation-fixture edits were assumed not to affect the benchmark runtime because the intended production delta appeared comment-only. An exact rebuild produced a different compressed Wasm identity, so the prior generated Weight artifacts could no longer attest the current source state.
remedy: After any source-tree mutation, rebuild and hash the benchmark runtime before retaining decision-bearing artifacts; if the Wasm identity changes, rerun every coupled benchmark sequentially even when the edit was believed semantically inert.

title: Additive FRAME model hid an Actor-count by Predicate-count interaction
summary: The first EXP-0025 Transfer benchmark varied C32 Actor count and per-Actor Predicate count as independent linear components even though Predicate reads scale with their product. The generated additive n+p model attributed only a fixed p term and could not soundly charge the n×p workload.
remedy: Hold per-Actor geometry fixed whenever its cost repeats across a population component; benchmark Predicate 0/2/4 as separate n-scaled branches rather than fitting an additive two-component model without an interaction term.

title: Detached frame service mistaken for atomic successor placement
summary: The first EXP-0025 retry path took the Ready chunk out of storage, committed execution and a same-page Continuation inside a per-Actor transaction, then rewrote the stale local source frame and aggregate occupancy after the transaction. This erased the committed Continuation while leaving its tail and locator published.
remedy: Keep the source chunk resident; consume the exact source slot and decrement occupancy inside the same per-Actor storage transaction that executes and places the successor. Let successor append restore occupancy, retain open partial ranges, and advance the Ready head across a fully closed empty ticket range.

title: Ordinary Running mistaken for retry continuation telemetry
summary: The first EXP-0025 Running branch emitted CycleContinued for every ordinary persisted next Step because the event name appeared to describe all Continuations. A0 emits that event only when a Suspended retry begins; ordinary Running advances without it, so the candidate introduced event drift despite matching state and effects.
remedy: Treat event ownership as executable semantics rather than lexical implication. Differential-test each Running and Suspended transition against A0 event sequences; emit CycleContinued only on the existing Suspended retry path.

title: Terminal Running parity mistaken for middle-Step parity
summary: The two-Step EXP-0025 differential covered Opening and terminal Running only, so both paths updated last_cycle_block at a completion boundary and concealed that the candidate also advanced it during an ordinary nonterminal continuation. A three-Step differential exposed the one-block drift.
remedy: For multi-Step state machines, compare Opening, at least one nonterminal middle transition, and terminal completion independently; do not infer middle-state parity from matching terminal snapshots.

title: Frame geometry mistaken for the middle-Step proof owner
summary: The first continuation follow-up treated source and successor C32 frames as the likely owner of the 100-Actor middle-Step miss. The generated storage ledger showed a 6,553-byte per-Actor slope and a 6,545-byte ActorContractTailChunk proof addition, while frame chunks were cohort-level keys.
remedy: Read the generated per-storage proof ledger before changing the visually salient geometry; attribute the slope to key cardinality and maximum value proof, then route optimization to the owning representation experiment.

title: Maximum storage annotation mistaken for actual workload proof
summary: EXP-0004 initially inferred that reducing ActorContractTailChunk capacity from four Steps to two would reduce the 6,545-byte annotated maximum proof. The three-Step workload stores two actual tail Steps under both capacities, so its encoded value and generated 6,553-byte slope remained identical; one-Step splitting added a key and regressed proof.
remedy: Distinguish storage metadata maxima from the actual values materialized by a measured workload. Run the smallest capacity control before planning lifecycle work, and count all keys loaded by complete-context reconstruction.

title: Compact execution payload mistaken for removal of the canonical tail owner
summary: EXP-0004 C3 removed ActorContractTailChunk from Running control-context reconstruction and added one compact current payload, but complete-path Weight still read canonical tail geometry during exact User state-hold reconciliation. The candidate therefore added a key and regressed grouped proof to 7,103.24 instead of removing the owner.
remedy: Trace every downstream owner after a representation substitution, including economic state-hold reconciliation. Do not combine a separately accepted hold optimization with a Step-layout candidate; reject the candidate or open a separately controlled mechanism experiment.

title: State-hold tail scan mistaken for the sole full-Contract execution owner
summary: EXP-0027 removed immutable Contract-body scans from per-Step state-hold reconciliation, but the maximum 12-Step path still read all three tail chunks because execution-plan construction independently requested full Contract reconstruction. Candidate and baseline therefore retained identical 11 reads/Actor and 9,882 estimated proof/Actor slopes.
remedy: Before changing one apparent scan owner, enumerate every call site that requests the same storage keys and measure an exact baseline owner. A cache or scan elision is material only if no independently retained path reproduces the same read/proof set.

title: Trigger fee-collection failure mistaken for one family-uniform rollback rule
summary: The staged C1 temporal latch initially rolled back both AtTime and Cadenced fee-collection failure. A0 evidence distinguishes them: AtTime preserves its one-shot due reference for retry, while Cadenced consumes the failed occurrence and advances to the next deadline without readiness or apoptosis.
remedy: Treat failure semantics as Trigger-family contract, not a shared helper default. Differentially test retained detector authority after failure: AtTime retries the same due occurrence; Cadenced advances its deadline and remains unlatched.

title: try_mutate inventory mistaken for complete hot-mutation ownership
summary: The first C1 cutover inventory centralized ActorHot::try_mutate, insert, remove, and ordinary reads but omitted seven production ActorHot::mutate call sites in zero-Step, Opening, continuation, failure-streak, paused-head, and stale-ticket paths. Claims that every production hot mutation was behind seams were therefore too broad.
remedy: Inventory every StorageMap mutation form (`mutate`, `try_mutate`, `mutate_exists`, `try_mutate_exists`, `insert`, `remove`, `set`, `take`) before declaring single-owner cutover readiness. Keep infallible fallback semantics in a dedicated owner seam rather than treating only fallible mutations as authority.

title: Pre-consumption Actor view mistaken for post-Opening hot state
summary: Cadenced rearm initially copied the Ready source ticket from the frozen ActiveActorView into the post-Opening transition. The scalar transition had already cleared that ticket, so the next recurrence rolled back even though the Trigger and admission authority were correct.
remedy: Freeze semantic identity, Contract, admission, and Trigger state before source consumption, but explicitly normalize transition-owned hot fields to their post-Opening values. For Cadenced rearm retain the consumed latch context needed by recurrence placement while clearing the consumed Ready ticket before publishing the next reference.

title: Scalar active-existence check mistaken for collision safety
summary: ActorId admission still classified occupancy through scalar active state after canonical identity moved to frame control. If scalar identity/hot/admission differentials were absent, an existing frame-owned Actor could appear vacant and permit attempted identity reuse.
remedy: Every identity-allocation and collision boundary must query the canonical active owner, not a differential projection. Prove an active frame primary remains occupied after all scalar control partitions are removed and rejects creation at the same ActorId without mutation.

title: Frame service loader mistaken for drop-in placement authority
summary: Replacing the scalar loader inside prime_actor_schedule with the current frame service loader passed an Unsignaled smoke test but broke paused Cadenced resume, suspended-run placement, paused Crossing coalescing, and exact QueueTicket exhaustion rollback after Contract replacement or run cancellation. Frame primary hot state still preserves source ticket or physical wakeup authority that the transitional scalar post-consumption projection has already cleared, so the same planner input is not yet equivalent.
remedy: Do not globally substitute frame loading at placement boundaries until each caller passes its explicit normalized post-consumption hot snapshot plus source-consumed and destination-publication facts. Preserve the scalar bridge for prime_actor_schedule, and convert paused, retry, cancellation, replacement, and temporal transitions atomically before removing it.

title: Post-take frame loading mistaken for wakeup source authority
summary: A global Block-wakeup switch loaded canonical frame service state only after taking the Actor-bearing WakeupPages slot. Unsignaled terminal/reference validation intentionally requires that physical pointer to remain live, so the loader rejected valid source authority; low-level arbitrary Idle/unlatched Block-wakeup fixtures additionally exposed geometry that canonical C1 does not admit.
remedy: Freeze and validate frame authority while the selected WakeupPages reference is still physically present, then consume source and publish a normalized destination in one transaction. Convert or retire arbitrary Idle/unlatched service-wakeup fixtures instead of weakening C1 restoration or silently falling back to scalar authority.

title: Strict active projection mistaken for drop-in scalar replacement
summary: Switching the legacy active_actor_view helper globally to strict frame loading made the new admissionless completion witness pass but initially broke scalar-oriented fixture mutations, exhaustion setup, observation activation, and simulation expectations across eleven tests. The one-line substitution was unsafe; the later retained cutover required migrating the complete caller/fixture cohort and separating simulation-only post-effect reconstruction from live frame projection.
remedy: Keep strict frame consumers explicit through load_actor_state_for_frame_control until every caller and fixture has representation-honest authority. Migrate the projection boundary with its complete caller set, normalize terminal Failed and window-expiry destinations, coalesce busy frame primaries in place, and reconstruct simulation-only post-effect state from its loaded hot snapshot rather than using one witness to justify a global loader swap.

title: Run source-consumed flag mistaken for all placement consumption
summary: Cancellation can invalidate a live wakeup and consume its Waiting frame primary even when the caller-level source_consumed flag is false; treating that flag as complete placement provenance removes required Unsignaled restoration and makes deactivation fail closed.
remedy: Carry one closed cancellation mode—retained scalar, retained frame, consumed scalar, or consumed frame—across nested wakeup invalidation. Restoration and nonce publication derive from that mode instead of one overloaded source-consumed flag or an order-sensitive boolean pair.

title: Selected control mode mistaken for commit-time authority availability
summary: Activation commit initially reloaded frame admission solely because the preflight-selected mode was frame, while scalar-fixture terminal activation was routed through a strict frame-validating close wrapper. Mode selects semantics but does not prove a primary remains readable across every placement-changing commit, and direct scalar transitions still require their supplied loaded snapshot.
remedy: Carry the selected mode and any required frame admission in ActivationPlan from preflight to commit. Frame close consumes the frozen certificate; explicit scalar close consumes its loaded scalar snapshot directly instead of reopening the global strict projection.

title: Activation source mode mistaken for destination publication mode
summary: Passing one scalar/frame flag through unified activation made ordinary direct scalar fixtures stop publishing their required C1 mirror, diverging from compact ObservationChange even though both returned Latched. Source authority selection and destination publication coincide in production and combined isolation but intentionally differ in ordinary differential tests.
remedy: Capture source loading and destination publication as separate facts at the activation wrapper. Let ActivationPlan own publication and frozen frame admission; direct scalar atoms may load scalar state while ordinary tests still publish C1, and combined benchmark isolation selects scalar for both.

title: Frame Waiting coordinates mistaken for physical wakeup-pointer coordinates
summary: C1 Waiting publication overwrote the already allocated physical WakeupPages pointer with the independent frame chunk page/slot. Small package fixtures accidentally aligned both namespaces, while the 512-Actor runtime mixed-clock test diverged after genesis tombstones and faulted every Tick occurrence.
remedy: Treat ActorControlLocation as the frame address and ActorHot wakeup pointers as lightweight physical WakeupPages references. Preserve the allocated physical pointer through Waiting publication, match source consumption by validated clock/key, and test with populations where the two page/slot namespaces necessarily diverge.

title: Transaction-local scalar projection mistaken for retained differential authority
summary: Frame-only temporal execution correctly used a temporary scalar hot projection after Ready source consumption, but cycle-nonce commit unconditionally recreated scalar identity and successful destination publication retained the temporary hot partition. Functional execution passed while the supposedly absent scalar control geometry silently returned.
remedy: Stable identity commit updates a surviving primary and an already existing differential only; source-consumed frame execution may create only the retained execution core's transaction-local hot bridge when no primary survives; frame-destination nonce commit never creates an absent scalar identity differential. The placement transaction must freeze pre-transition identity/hot/admission differential presence independently before source consumption, pass that typed fact explicitly instead of inferring from the temporary bridge, and remove transaction-local bridges after successful frame destination publication and state-hold reconciliation across every Trigger family. Loaded User execution must defer state-hold reconciliation while only a transaction-local hot projection exists, then reconcile from the surviving frame destination. Suspended retry now removes the transaction-local bridge after frame Waiting publication; exact window expiry freezes and consumes that complete Waiting source, then closes directly from supplied authority without transient Ready publication.

title: Multi-block test helper mistaken for a single-block Q1 witness
summary: The partial-differential matrix initially used run_idle to assert a middle-Step state. That helper intentionally advances additional blocks while any scalar ActorHot remains Running, so hot-retained cases completed Step 1 before the assertion and appeared to violate one-Step-per-block execution while frame-only cases stopped after Step 0.
remedy: Use one explicit on_idle call for a single-block assertion, then advance block/on_initialize/prepass/on_idle deliberately. Independently guard service against a loaded Running head whose last_committed_step_block already equals now so Q1 does not depend only on test helpers or queue-cutoff geometry.

title: Exact-next retry mistaken for Block Waiting
summary: A frame-only RetryLater witness initially expected cooldown-one retry to own a Block wakeup. Canonical scheduling intentionally keeps an exact N+1 retry in Ready with eligible_at=N+1; only later backoff or earlier terminal-window substitution belongs to Block Waiting.
remedy: Assert no Block wakeup for exact-next retry, preserve the immutable Ready ticket and frame-owned Run authority, snapshot the next block cutoff in prepass, then execute at the eligible block. Test later backoff and terminal-window substitution separately through Block Waiting.

title: Retained Ready close mistaken for consumed-source finalization
summary: Ready admission selected underfunded User apoptosis before queue consumption, but loaded finalization labeled every frame close as source-consumed and supplied no source state. Frame-only retry therefore could not cancel its live Run and left the Actor active while scalar-backed tests passed.
remedy: Carry the closed cancellation mode into finalization. A Ready pre-consumption close must use RetainedFrame with complete loaded state/admission; a physically consumed Waiting close uses ConsumedFrame. Perform queue-owner removal only inside the retained close transaction and prove custody neutrality, fee absence, hold release, and scalar absence.

title: Due temporal placement failure mistaken for retained-source exhaustion close
summary: The shared scheduler-index close was correctly changed to retain a live primary, then was incorrectly reused after due Tick consumption. Cadenced rearm exhaustion had already consumed its physical Waiting source, so retained reload could not close and left scalar identity behind.
remedy: Choose cancellation mode from actual source transition, never close reason. General placement exhaustion with a live primary uses the retained frame/scalar owner; due temporal placement or rearm failure uses ConsumedFrame with the frozen post-source state. Keep the scalar benchmark branch explicit.

title: Supplied frame wakeup transition reopened scalar invalidation
summary: Observation future activation carried complete frame identity, hot state, admission, cursor, and resource authority but the authority-native wakeup helper still called the scalar-loading invalidator when replacing an existing terminal pointer. With scalar control removed, Unsignaled Block-201 to Waiting Block-10 placement failed as corrupted topology.
remedy: Invalidate the validated physical pointer directly from supplied hot authority, clear the selected clock locally, commit that cleared hot state to any retained primary, then perform source-to-destination placement with supplied identity, cursor, admission, and resources. Preserve the compact scalar fixture by making admission optional outside frame mode.

title: Cadenced Opening rearm mistaken for a standalone frame destination
summary: Replacing the loaded Cadenced Opening rearm bridge with immediate authority-native Waiting publication passed simple cadence tests but rolled back busy Running preservation. Rearm occurs inside the same consumed-Ready execution transaction whose successor must carry both service and Trigger authority; publishing an independent early destination changed that coupled persistence geometry.
remedy: Keep the transitional rearm bridge until direct frame execution owns the entire source-consume, Trigger-pointer update, Step commit, and final successor publication as one state transition. Do not promote rearm to a standalone destination before replacing the retained execution core.

title: Final scalar absence mistaken for no transient scalar materialization
summary: Earlier frame-only execution witnesses checked that scalar hot was absent after completion, but Ready consumption still created a transaction-local hot bridge and cleanup removed it later. Final storage geometry alone did not prove single-owner mutation throughout the transaction.
remedy: Instrument the exact Ready-consume materialization seam. Suppress materialization before direct frame execution, mutate frozen state locally, publish the sole destination, and require the counter to remain zero in addition to final scalar absence. Apply this proof separately to each execution family before deleting the bridge globally.

title: Coupled Trigger rearm mistaken for requiring a scalar execution bridge
summary: Standalone early Cadenced Waiting publication was correctly rejected, but that did not imply Cadenced or ObservationCrossing zero-Step Opening required scalar hot. Both can mutate their physical Trigger topology and return a local successor hot projection inside the consumed-Ready transaction, leaving publication to the single final execution destination.
remedy: Separate Trigger-topology mutation from owner publication. Apply wakeup or membership replacement transaction-locally to frozen authority, return the updated hot projection, and publish only the final execution successor. Prove the materialization counter remains zero and try-state validates the retained topology.

title: Current-Step admission fee mistaken for resource-only maximum fee
summary: The first direct StopCycle path initially compared the loaded plan fee with maximum_current_step_fee, but canonical execution validates the exact Step-aware maximum_current_action_fee. The resource-only envelope is not the admitted action-fee identity even when StopCycle has no economic effect.
remedy: Direct current-Step implementations must replay the canonical Step-aware admission check against the loaded Step and its resource certificate. Use resource-only maximums for broad reservation, never as a substitute for the admitted action-fee breakdown.

title: Running direct execution tempted to recapture Predicate state
summary: A Running Step already owns its Opening predicate vector and cursor in the persisted Run. Re-evaluating against current chain state during direct frame execution would violate snapshot semantics even though the Step has no economic effect.
remedy: Opening direct execution captures bounded Predicate results once. Running and Suspended direct slices must consume the Run-owned snapshot and cursor, advance bounded outcomes, and never recapture current Predicate state.

title: One-Step Suspended core mistaken for a general continuation core
summary: Promoting the candidate loaded-Step core and routing every Suspended RetryLater Step through it left a multi-Step continuation suspended: the Suspended branch intentionally admits only a one-Step Contract at cursor zero, while Running supports general cursors. The broad dispatcher selected a shape the core correctly rejected.
remedy: Route direct execution only across the core's proven semantic domain. Before widening Suspended support, generalize cursor validation, event indices, Predicate cursor advancement, continuation Run publication, and terminal behavior together, then add a multi-Step witness; never infer generality from a shared result type.

title: Non-execution Ready consumption mistaken for requiring scalar hot
summary: Paused dequeue, stale Step-ticket repair, and admission Skip historically materialized scalar hot because they reused an execution-era consume helper. Each transition already carried complete frozen identity, hot, Run, admission, and resource authority and performed no Step effect.
remedy: Classify source consumption independently from execution. For non-execution Ready transitions, consume the immutable ticket without scalar materialization, publish the classified frame successor from supplied authority, reconcile the surviving User hold, and prove zero bridge writes plus no cycle events.

title: Opening outcome mistaken for derivable from Predicate truth
summary: A direct Opening Step previously inferred the continuation's last outcome from Predicate truth after execution. ContinueNextStep proves that a true Predicate can still yield Executed, Failed, ResolutionSkipped, or FundingUnavailable, so Predicate truth is not an outcome owner.
remedy: Carry the typed StepOutcome from the exact prepare/effect branch into Run publication. Derive counters and last_step_outcome from that branch, never from Predicate truth or effect-invocation alone, and witness frame-only failure-to-continuation with zero scalar materialization.

title: Retry terminal failure mistaken for resuspension invariant failure
summary: The direct RetryLater core treated permanent adapter failure and a next attempt reaching max_attempts as impossible resuspensions. Returning an invariant would roll back consumed frame execution instead of publishing Failed/Idle or closing with RetryAttemptsExhausted.
remedy: Classify terminal retry before successor placement. Permanent failure commits Failed/Idle below the global threshold; local max-attempt exhaustion closes from consumed authority as RetryAttemptsExhausted; a simultaneous global streak limit closes as ConsecutiveFailures. Never route a terminal retry through suspension eligibility.

title: Frame direct execution mistaken for an incremental scalar-fixture cutover
summary: Allowing direct loaded-Step execution whenever a frame primary existed, even when a retained scalar hot differential also existed, switched twenty scalar-oracle and combined-fixture tests to Q1 frame semantics before their whole retained-tree substitution. Snapshot cardinality, same-pass suffix execution, FundingUnavailable events, and lifecycle timing diverged together.
remedy: Keep direct frame execution gated on absent scalar hot while combined fixtures remain intentional scalar authority. Remove that gate only in the same retained-tree substitution that rewrites scalar-oracle fixtures and deletes stale coexisting differentials; do not incrementally reinterpret mixed representation as frame authority.

title: Mutation authority mistaken for retained cancellation authority
summary: Contract replacement classified mixed scalar-differential fixtures as scalar for in-place mutation, then reused that mode for retained Run cancellation. Four semantic-control tests failed because the same Actors still had canonical frame primaries and cancellation had historically loaded that retained frame authority.
remedy: Keep Trigger/mutation authority and retained cancellation selection separate while scalar differentials coexist with frame primaries. Unify them only in the atomic retained-tree fixture substitution that removes mixed authority; do not infer cancellation source from a narrower in-place mutation gate.

title: Frame locator presence mistaken for valid surviving primary authority
summary: A typed state-hold helper classified frame authority from ActorControlLocators presence alone. Terminal Ready, wakeup-expiry, and Contract-replacement paths can retain a locator while the primary is consumed, malformed, or no longer readable, so four close paths failed or left the Actor active.
remedy: Select frame state-hold authority only when load_frame_control_authority validates a surviving primary. Locator presence is topology input, not proof of readable authority; consumed or invalid destinations must fall back to the explicit scalar/closed cleanup semantics.

title: Candidate wakeup coordinate compatibility removed before fixture cutover
summary: Removing the ScalarFixtureIsolation coordinate-alignment capability made two combined runtime-benchmark candidate transitions accept stale pre-positioned physical pointers instead of rejecting them. Due-page and Crossing rollback witnesses changed from typed invariant failure to successful movement.
remedy: Retain the explicit aligned-coordinate capability for combined scalar fixtures until their stale primaries and placement differentials are atomically rewritten. Frame and physical address spaces remain independent, but a fixture-supplied physical pointer must still identify its actual physical slot; do not broaden acceptance as an incremental cutover.
